title: Java Methods
learningObjectives: Describe a method as a named block of code that performs a task.
Identify a method's return type, name, parameter list and body.
Declare and call a static method from another method in the same class.
Use void when a method does not return a value.
Explain how methods improve reuse, decomposition and readability.

understand.concept: A method is a named block of statements that can be called when its work is needed. A method declaration specifies its return type, name, parameters and body. A method can return a value or use void when it completes an action without returning one.
understand.whyItMatters: Methods divide a program into smaller responsibilities. A well-named method can be reused and tested independently, reducing repeated code and making main easier to read.
understand.analogy: Think of a method as a named tool: give it the information it needs, let it perform one defined task, and use its result when appropriate.
understand.analogyLimit: A program follows exact language rules; a real-world tool may need judgment and safety checks that code must model explicitly.

explain.narrative:
## Method structure

A method declaration includes modifiers, a return type, a method name, parentheses and a body. For example, `static int add(int a, int b)` returns an integer.

## Calling methods

A call uses the method name and parentheses. When a method is declared `static`, it can be called from `main` in the same class without creating an object. Instance methods are called through an object; that distinction is explored with classes later.

## Return values and void

A non-void method must return a value compatible with its declared return type on every reachable path. A `void` method performs an action and does not return a value.

## Common mistakes

- Declaring a non-void method without returning a value.
- Writing a method call without parentheses.
- Confusing printing a value with returning a value.
- Defining a method inside another method.
